Habitable
HAB-ih-tuh-bul
a. (capable of being inhabited; fit for habitation or dwelling)
Latin habitabilis, from habitare, to dwell, itself from habere, to have or hold. The habitable part of a place is, at root, the part able to be held and dwelt in by living inhabitants.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Wisdom's own speech in Proverbs eight, describing her presence at the creation of the world before the mountains were settled or the fountains established, arrives at a striking claim about where her deepest delight was actually found: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men. Wisdom does not describe her joy as centered on the vast, uninhabited cosmos alone, the depths or the heavens or the foundations of the earth mentioned earlier in the same speech; her rejoicing narrows and focuses specifically on the habitable part, the portion of creation actually made for men to dwell in.

The parallel half of the verse makes the focus explicit: my delights were with the sons of men. Wisdom, present with God before any of the world's works of old, as one brought up with him, daily his delight, chooses in the very same breath to locate her own delight not merely in the grandeur of the whole created order but specifically in the habitable earth made for human dwelling and in mankind itself. It is a striking claim for a book devoted mostly to practical instruction: the divine Wisdom that helped establish the entire cosmos found her particular joy exactly where ordinary people actually live, work, and dwell, rather than in some more rarefied or inaccessible corner of creation.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): capable of being inhabited; suitable for the residence of human beings.

expand to see more

HABITABLE, a. Capable of being inhabited; fit to be dwelt in; suitable for residence.

REJOICE, v.i. To feel joy or gladness in a high degree; to exult; to be delighted.

WISDOM, n. The right use of knowledge; the faculty of discerning and pursuing the best ends by the best means, personified in Proverbs as present at creation.

FOUNDATION, n. The base or lower part of a structure; figuratively, the fixed and original establishment of the earth.

DELIGHT, n. A high degree of pleasure or satisfaction of mind; joy taken in a person or thing.

Key Scripture

Pro 8:22 — "The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old."

Pro 8:30 — "Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;"

Pro 8:31 — "Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men."

Isa 45:18 — "For thus saith the LORD that created the heavens; God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else."

Modern Corruption

Wisdom is imagined as an abstract, detached faculty removed from ordinary human life, when Proverbs eight has Wisdom herself declare her deepest delight to be located precisely in the habitable earth and among the sons of men.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition of the plain word; habitable still names what is fit for dwelling. The principle worth recovering is the deliberate focus of Wisdom's own testimony in this passage. Having just described her presence before the mountains, the fountains, and the foundations of the earth, she narrows her rejoicing specifically to the habitable part, the portion actually made for human dwelling, rather than resting her delight in creation's grandest or least accessible reaches.

Isaiah's later statement supplies the theology behind Wisdom's own preference: God formed the earth not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited. A habitable world is not a lesser or incidental byproduct of creation but part of its original purpose, and Wisdom's delight in that habitable earth and in the sons of men who dwell there models the same priority the LORD Himself is said to have built into creation from the start.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tebel (H8398), the habitable world, the earth as a dwelling place; the noun behind “the habitable part” in Proverbs 8:31.

expand to see more

Hebrew tebel (H8398) — the habitable world, the earth considered as a dwelling place; the noun rendered “the habitable part” in Proverbs 8:31.

Hebrew sha'shua (H8191) — delight, pleasure; the noun behind “delights” in the same verse, Wisdom's own joy.

Hebrew qanah (H7069) — to possess, acquire, or bring forth; the verb behind “possessed me” in Proverbs 8:22.

Hebrew amon (H542, disputed) — a master workman, or one brought up; the term describing Wisdom's own relationship to the LORD in verse 30.

Hebrew yatsar (H3335) — to form, to fashion; the verb behind Isaiah 45:18's declaration that the earth was formed to be inhabited.

Usage

"“Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men” — Wisdom's own declared joy."

"“I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him” — Wisdom's standing before the LORD at creation."

"“he formed it to be inhabited” — the theology behind a habitable earth as God's own original intent."
